# javaabu/mobile-verification

> Mobile number login, registration and verification with one-time SMS codes for Laravel, built on javaabu/auth v3: mobile login is a javaabu/auth LoginMethod of any user type (two-factor authentication still applies), mobile registration ends in a javaabu/stencil details form, signed-in users verify or change their number on an account page, and `mobile.verified` guards pages that need one. Codes are hashed, expire, are limited by a resend interval, lock the number after too many wrong entries, and are rate limited per IP. SMS through javaabu/sms-notifications, Sanctum/Passport tokens and a Passport `mobile` grant for apps, admin actions behind javaabu/permissions permissions. Pages in Blade (javaabu/forms) and Inertia React (@javaabu/forms), in Dhivehi and right to left.

Paths are relative to this file. In a project, that's vendor/javaabu/mobile-verification/.

## Rules

- Set up javaabu/auth user types first. Turn on mobile login per type with `'login_methods' => [Javaabu\MobileVerification\Auth\MobileLoginMethod::class]` in `config('javaabu-auth.user_types')`, or `MobileVerification::enableFor('user')` before the routes load. `Route::authRoutes()` then registers `login.mobile…` (and `register.mobile…` for types with javaabu/auth's `registration` feature) with the type's route-name prefix (`admin.login.mobile`).
- Don't write mobile login or OTP controllers by hand. Customise with a controller from `config('mobile-verification.controllers')` (extend the package's), the `CreatesUsersFromMobileNumbers`, `GeneratesVerificationCodes` and `ValidatesNumberFormat` bindings, the `registration_form` stencil class, or the `notification` class.
- The mobile login finishes with javaabu/auth's `StartAuthenticatedSession`, so two-factor users get the challenge; `skip_two_factor` opts out. Never call `Auth::login()` for a mobile login.
- User models implement `Javaabu\MobileVerification\Contracts\HasMobileNumber` with `Javaabu\MobileVerification\Concerns\InteractsWithMobileNumbers`. One verified number per user (`phone` relation, `mobile_numbers` table, morph `user`). Users of different types may share a number. Tables of types with mobile registration need nullable `password` (and `email` with the default form): `UserSchema::columns($table, password_required: false, email_required: false)`.
- Change a user's number in code with `updateMobileNumber()`/`updatePhone()`/`removeMobileNumber()`; users change their own on `Route::mobileNumberRoutes('user')` (`settings/mobile-number`, route `mobile-number`), which checks a code; the package adds it to javaabu/auth's account navigation (`UserTypes::accountLink('mobile-number', …)`, shown for types with the route; change it with `UserTypes::get($type)->accountLink()` / `withoutAccountLink('mobile-number')`). Protect pages that need a number with `mobile.verified:{type}` after `auth.type:{type}`.
- Send and check codes with `Actions\SendVerificationCode` and `Actions\VerifyVerificationCode` (they throw `ValidationException`); never compare codes yourself, store them in plain text, or check them in a validation rule (a wrong code counts as an attempt).
- Request fields are `number`, `country_code`, `verification_code`, `verification_code_id`; numbers are normalized (`077 712-34` → `7771234`, `+960` → `960`). Validate numbers with `Rules\IsValidMobileNumber` (`->registered()`, `->notRegistered()->ignore($user)`) and `Rules\IsValidCountryCode`.
- API clients use `Route::mobileApiRoutes('user')` (`POST api/mobile/code`, `POST api/mobile/token`, via javaabu/auth's `ApiTokens`) or the Passport `mobile` grant (user type from the client's provider).
- Admin actions come from `Route::mobileNumberActions('user', ['middleware' => ['web', 'auth.type:admin']])`, behind the `mobile-verification.update|unlock|remove` abilities taking `[$type, $account]` and the `{action}_{type}_mobile_numbers` permissions; run `php artisan permissions:sync`.
- Pages follow the user type's stack (`mobile-verification.views` overrides): Blade `mobile-verification::login`, …, React `mobile-verification::Login`, `Register`, `Verify`, `RegisterDetails`, `Settings/MobileNumber` through javaabu/manifest. Override with `vendor:publish --tag=mobile-verification-views` or `php artisan manifest:override mobile-verification <file>`.
- Every user-facing string is an English `__()` key with Dhivehi in `lang/dv.json`. Keep numbers and codes `dir="ltr"` and use logical utilities (`ms-`, `text-start`) only. In tests, `Notification::fake()` and read the code from `VerificationCodeNotification::$verification_code`.

- [Registration](docs/basic-usage/registration.md): the steps, routes, the stencil form, creating the user
